title: TEM Studies of Nanostructure in Aluminium-Copper Welds Made by Solid State Joining
content: Electrical conductors made from aluminum (Al) and copper (Cu) are of great interest in many applications such as power generation, transportation and electronic industry/busbars, as they combine the high electrical conductivity of Cu and light weight of Al and its alloys. However, welding of Al to Cu can be challenging due to their dissimilar thermophysical properties. High welding temperatures lead to formation of brittle intermetallic phases with high electrical resistivity at the weld interface. In addition, heat treatable Al alloys often lose strength when strengthening precipitate phases are exposed to high temperatures, leading to a heat affected zone (HAZ). The bimetallic welds should therefore be made with thin layers of intermetallic phases (IMPs) and low heat input. Characterization of microstructure and phases formed is needed to understand the process and be able to optimize welding conditions for strong metallurgical bonding.
